newsitem.title: USA: Elusive Brent finally offered into U.S. Gulf Coast.
newsitem.headline: Elusive Brent finally offered into U.S. Gulf Coast.

text.p: A string of North Sea Brent cargoes that had been bouncing around Europe and sowing confusion in the oil market this week finally showed signs of moving to the Gulf Coast on Friday, traders said.

Stasco, a division of Royal Dutch/Shell, was offering up to one million barrels of Brent into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP) at a discount of $1.10 to May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for May 1-10, traders said.
The price does not include lightering, which adds some 25-30 cents to the cost, traders said.
"I think it's a reasonably competitive price and a good alternative to LLS," said a Gulf Coast refiner, referring to the competing domestic grade Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James.
Traders pointed out that the Shell offer was unusual because the Anglo-Dutch company does not normally move Brent cargoes across the Atlantic.
"It's unusual, unless it's tied to something else," one buyer commented, alluding to a possible paper position.
Shell picked up eight Brent cargoes from British Petroleum on Thursday, and is likely to keep the bulk of the barrels in its own vast refining system, traders said.
The May spread between WTI/Cushing and Brent was around $1.35-40 a barrel Friday afternoon.
Transatlantic trade was deemed relatively attractive as freight rates gradually begin to soften.
The week's broad speculation over the fate of the Brent cargoes unsettled prices for short-haul and domestic sweet barrels, traders said.
Latin American crudes have been particularly hard hit in light of costly freight rates in the Caribbean.
Colombian Cusiana was last heard done at WTI minus $1.65-70 a barrel for May 1-2 loading, down 15-20 cents from recent values.
At least three Cusiana cargoes were on offer for second-half May loading, putting them out of direct competition with the Brent cargoes, traders said.
Elsewhere in Latin America, Chile's state-owned oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo (ENAP) bought 360,000 barrels of Ecuadoran Oriente crude from Ecuadoran broker Tripetrol for May 20 delivery.
The crude was sold at an undisclosed discount to WTI.
Meanwhile, Argentina's YPF was offering two 400,000 barrel cargoes fo Canadon Seco and one 400,000 barrel cargo of Escalante for April loading, traders said.
From West Africa, a U.S. company was offering Nigerian Qua Iboe to the Gulf Coast at dated Brent plus $1.75 a barrel for mid- to late May.
A U.S. broker was showing Palanca for May 5-10 delivery at June WTI minus 25 cents, traders said.
Gulf Coast buyers were seen as finicky as oil prices continue to decline.
"The mentality is to sit back and wait for prices to come to you," one trader noted.
Another trader suggested that buyers still have plenty of choices. "I think people are getting very accustommed to good pickings."
--Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
